To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current experimental data allow a model-independent determination of alpha in the range (0, 2pi) and that the charge-averaging procedure is not a sufficient tool to extract alpha from B-->pipi data.

the current data on B-d-->pi(+/-)pi(0), B-d-->pi(pi), and B-d(0)/(0)-->pi(pi) decay modes allow us to constrain the parameter space of CP violation and that the weak phase alpha is directly related to the charge-averaging branching fractions and CP asymmetries of these transitions.

(a) direct CP violation in the B-d-->pi+pi- decay mode is strongly correlated with the B-d-->pipi CP asymmetries, (b) direct CP violation is strongly correlated with isospin triangles and (c) the B-d-->pizero pizero decay mode is crucial in the isospin analysis
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isospin analysis and the direct CP violation in the B-->pipi system.
the study of CP violation in B-meson decays.
the study of the direct CP asymmetry in the decay B-d-->pi+pi-.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are consistent with a vanishing direct CP violation in the B-->pipi sector, but the current data are not sufficient to exclude the possibility of sizable direct CP violation in this sector.
the current experimental situation is not yet conclusive.
the data do not yet rule out any of the possible values of alpha, and therefore, the present situation is similar to the one before the observation of B-->pi pi decays in 1999.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current experimental data on direct CP violation in these decays can be well described by the Standard Model.
a combined measurement of these observables can determine alpha with a 5% precision, which is the best precision ever achieved by a single experiment.
, in the presence of direct CP violation, the isospin triangles for B-d-->pipi decaying modes are not closed and the CP-conservation hypothesis can be tested in B-->pipi modes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a measurement of B-s(0)-->pipi branching ratios and CP-violating rates can shed light on the nature of alpha.
the isospin triangles for B-->pipi are not closed and thus the CP-conserving hypothesis is not yet ruled out.
a measurement of B-d-->pi(+/-)pi(-/+) with a precision better than 0.1% will be able to determine alpha with an error of 0.5 degrees or less, which will provide a crucial test of the standard model.
